Dans un monde en pleine mutation, où les journaux « gÉPraissent et disparaissenfa i ^^ gré des goûts du lectorat et surtout de la rentabilité des investissements, un tel événement est rare. Il mérite d'être fêté, avec simplicité mais ferveur. Outre la reconnaissance due à toutes celles et à tous ceux qui ont contribué à maintenir le cap, cet anniversaire est également l'occasion pour le comité de rédaction actuel d'exprimer sa foi en l'avenir. Il le fait en publiant une petite plaquette qui résume l'histoire d'un journal qui, depuis un siècle, se consacre à la promotion de la paix, au rapprochement entre les humains et à leur compréhension réciproque. Ce centième anniversaire doit aussi être une occasion de réunir les lectrices et les lecteurs de l'Essor pour leur permettre de se connaître, de dialoguer et de s'enrichir. The Bands of Hope marched to St. George's square to form in processional order. The waggons were decorated for prizes, and awards were likewise given for the best. groomed horses. This Company has been formed to meft a long-recognised want. It will enable persons to furnish their apartments or houses with the money they would otherwise have to pay as rent. A married couple, occupying furnished apartments at a weekly rental of 305., or £7B per annum, might have similar apartments, unfurniihed, at £3O per annum. The use ot furniture, therefore, costs them £4B a year, whereas the cost of furnishing would not exceed £loo—which being provided, a saving of £4B per annum would be effected. The Equitable Furnishing Company will effect thi- saving, by supplying the furniture'the best of its kind, at ready-money prices, the party making his election to purchase at the end of a year and a half, two years, or three years. In the meantime, the furniture will be taken on hire, the hire being periodically paid. The whole of the payments will be allowed in the event of purchase, and thus the money which would have gone as rent will have bought the furniture. The charge made by the Company will be 7i per cent. per annum on the price of the goods, if purchased at the end of 18 months; of 8i per cent., if at the end of two years; and of 10 per cent., if at the end of three years. The Company will retain the ownership of all furniture until it has been paid for, so that any appropriation of it would constitute a criminal offence. Seizure for rent is the only adverse contingency to which the Company will be exposed; but as the deposit payable will always cover the first rent due, that risk will be small, and it is allowed for in the estimate of profits., The Directors have secured an established and first-rate furniture business, returning net profits of more than 20 per cent., with unusually commodious and admirably adapted premises, in one of the best situations at the West-end of the town, and a large stock s f well-seasoned furniture, exhibited in suites of apartments, in various styles. This will constitute a very advantageous basis for the Company's own business, and justifies the Directors in anticipating for the shareholders, after liberally providing for all possible contingencies, interest at the rate of at leaa 20 per cent. per annum.
